Digest 9.2.27. **MOM.** The Moon is argued for its inconstancy in a miraculous way; for it is sometimes whole, sometimes half, waxing, waning, silent, curved with horns. And for this reason the Doctors are poorly regarded, because they feel, disagree, distinguish, and divide things into a thousand atoms, not without great cost to the readers. And so, just as those conceived under the Moon fall into the falling sickness, as Quintus Serenus is the author, and those who spend a long time under the Moon fall into delirium, and are called "lunatics" by the jurist in Digest 21.1.1.8, so for the most part, those who follow the trifles and empty disputations of the Doctors everywhere fall into total folly, as those which were invented concerning the "extremes from which" and "extremes to which" in Digest 41.3.31. Likewise, those things concerning direct and common words in the treatise on substitutions. These are the inconveniences of the changeable Moon, which, although it ought to dispel the darkness of the night, as you said in the authentication *Ut iudicia*, section 2, column 2, it doubles the greater darkness, even if it has little to do with the matter. I will seem to you to invade the Stoa, to burn down the Academy, to demolish the Peripatetic school, if I disagree with Bartolus or with the common opinion of others. However, I cannot agree with Bartolus, who thinks that a donation was once a named contract, and is even much more so today, nor with the remaining interpreters, who indeed wish it to be named today, but not formerly, but, what you might wonder at, I assert even after Code 8.53.35 that a donation is an unnamed contract.

Bartolus objects to Digest 39.5.1, where in a donation there is no place for repentance; in unnamed contracts there is, Digest 12.4.3. To which it is commonly responded that no unnamed convention that is not reciprocal admits of repentance after tradition, and it is true.

The same Bartolus falsely notes that a donation takes its name from execution and from the thing handed over, by the example of a loan, a bailment, and a deposit, because a donation is a "giving of a gift," Digest 39.5.1. Therefore, he says, unless it is by the thing itself, it does not produce an action, although it had an elegant name. But that a donation existed before tradition is demonstrated by the said Code 8.53.35, "that it not be useless," as is wont to be said about permutation. I prove that it is entirely unnamed by these little reasons: because it has neither its own name, nor its own action. For it lies so wide that it contains a stipulation made without cause, Digest 39.5.1. But it lacks an action, because there is nowhere an action. For what action competes for a donation in the said section 5 of the law *Si quis argentum*, it is called by law. For I did not discuss them in such a way as to affirm that some exist, or to prove through adduced arguments that it is likely. On the contrary, I said that I would refrain from writing more about the kind of astronomy that would exist for the inhabitants of Saturn, precisely because most people consider it too absurd for men to live on planets; and therefore, they would say that I was wasting my time investigating what those might observe who do not exist in the nature of things. However, when I named the months of the Saturnians while calculating the period of the Saturnian Moon, I did nothing new or unusual for astronomers, for whom nothing is more common than to imagine that someone exists on the Sun or Moon, and from there observes the motions of the stars. There was no reason for Fabrius to blame me for having proposed this invention about Saturnians there. And even if it were otherwise, I would be neither the first to have put this forward, nor would it be so ridiculous, at least among philosophers, as he thinks. But I shall not digress into these matters beyond my established purpose. The contemplation of the Fabrian System calls me, namely that one by which, after he demolished mine, he trusts that the phenomena around Saturn can be conveniently explained. For those earlier arguments, by which he attempts to order the motion of Saturn itself with new laws, are irrelevant here, and it would not be worth the effort to examine them. I wonder, however, what displeased him in the Tychonic hypothesis, to make him decide to build a new one from its foundations: one which I fear astronomers can hardly grasp, let alone approve.

<margin>Inventor of medicine.</margin>
> Your grandfather, O Asclepius, was the first inventor of medicine, to whom a temple is consecrated on the mountain of Libya, near the shore of the crocodiles, in which his worldly man lies, that is, his body; for the remainder, or rather the whole—if a man is whole in mind—the better part of life, has returned to heaven.

What can be said more clearly, what more solidly to establish the immortality of the soul? It is evident, therefore, from the very true theology of *Mercury*, that *the human soul is immortal, and that man, not without the great counsel of the Creator, consists of a dual nature.* The text follows.
<margin>The text is explained.</margin>
For he is immortal, as it has been said, and he possesses the will of all things: *both because they are subject to his authority, and also because he can have knowledge of all things.* But other living beings, which are mortal, suffer by being subject to fate, because they serve the course of the stars
<margin>Fate.</margin>
and have no faculty of free will: for the wise man dominates the stars. I have spoken more broadly
<margin>The wise man dominates the stars.</margin>
*on fate in the 4th Pymander.* Man is therefore superior to harmony: that is, the soul, which is of a more divine order, having fallen into harmony, namely the lower one, that is, into the body, having been endangered, has been made a servant: for all danger stems from the bond of matter, and all trouble of unjust servitude stems from the commerce of the body. Here, fortified by the fecundity of both sexes, that is, endowed with the fecundity and abundance of procreating offspring, by Him who is the fountain of both sexes, that is, by God—as he had said a little earlier that God is most full of the fecundity of both sexes: which he certainly elucidates most openly in the *Asclepius*:
<margin>What both sexes signify in God.</margin>
> God, he says, is the only one like all things: most full of the fecundity of both sexes, always pregnant with His own will: He always brings forth whatever He wills to procreate in God: His will is all goodness: this same goodness of all things is born from the nature of His divinity, so that all things may be as they are and have been, and that nature may suffice from itself for all things that will be born hereafter: this is the reason how all things of both sexes come to be.

<margin>The good of fecundity.</margin>
For it is impossible for any of the animals that exist to be unfecund. Since, therefore, God is most full of the fecundity of both sexes—partly, because *His intellect and will are fecund, as I said in the beginning of the second Pymander;* partly also because He provides fecundity for others to bring forth and procreate—it behooves each of us to be fecund not so much in offspring as in virtues: for by this fecundity of both sexes, anyone ought to be fortified, namely, both with the charity of the will and the truth of the intellect; for the offspring of the will is love: but of the intellect, it is truth: and he was made watchful
<margin>The text is explained.</margin>
by Him who is watchful, he is contained and subjected to His dominion. Indeed, not only was man gifted with the bounty of fecundity by his Creator, but also with the grace of being watchful by Him who constantly keeps watch over His works:
> For He does not sleep, nor does He slumber, who guards Israel:

<margin>Man ought to be watchful.</margin>
For it is in man’s interest to be vigilant, lest, burdened by ignorance or the sleep of sloth, he lose himself and his own, which have been granted to him from heaven. He ought to clearly understand how he was created by God, and how he received many things from Him, to whose dominion he is subject, both by nature and by the gifts of grace; and therefore he must be very watchful, so that he may be pleasing and dear to Him under whose dominion he is contained.

However, he himself expresses the true occasion shortly in the preface, because he saw many things being written by many, which were not sufficiently verified; and therefore he wanted to provide for posterity through his own work, so that the Church might have a verified and solid Evangelical history. And Eusebius (book 3, chapter 24), Epiphanius (book 2 against heresies), and Nicephorus acknowledge this occasion.

<margin>Argument: Luke started the history of the Gospel higher up than the others, etc.</margin>
He begins the Evangelical history higher up than the other two did, namely Matthew and Mark, who, with Luke, pursue the history of humanity above all. For not content to start the matter from the baptism of John and the genealogy of Christ, he also takes up those things that pertain to the conception of both Christ and John the Baptist: likewise the birth of both, and what happened in these times. From here he finally progresses to the doctrine of Christ; likewise, what he did. In miracles, he is diligent and copious; for he indicates the occasions, the fruits, and other circumstances. He adorns the life of Christ with human affections, and those ready to gratify, so that sin is absent: he everywhere assigns companions to Christ, disciples who are extremely simple, or crowds eager to learn: adversaries who are extremely persistent, the Jews, and from these, the Pharisees, the Chief Priests

כתיב הכא בפקוד אתם וכתיב התם בפקוד אתם. 
מה להלן חשיבות אף כאן חשיבות. 
אמר רב אשי שמע מינה האי מאן דבעי למימני ישראל לא לימנינהו בגולגולתא. 
דכתיב לא יהיה בהם נגף בפקוד אתם. 
אמר רב יצחק כל המונה את ישראל עובר בלא תעשה. 
שנאמר ומספר בני ישראל יהיה כחול הים אשר לא ימד ולא יספר. 
אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק איכא דאמרי לא ימד ולא יספר. 
תניא ר' יצחק אומר מאי דכתיב ויתן את הכסף כופר נפשו. 
מלמד שכל אחד ואחד נותן מחצית השקל. 
מאי טעמא אמר רב אסי כדי שיכפרו על מעשה העגל. 
דכתיב ויתן את הכסף כופר נפשו לה' בפקוד אתם. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב מאי דכתיב ואתם תהיו לי ממלכת כהנים וגוי קדוש. 
אלו הדברים אשר תדבר אל בני ישראל. 
אמר רב חנינא בר פפא מאי דכתיב ויקח משה את האהל ונטה לו מחוץ למחנה. 
מלמד שהיה משה רבינו עליו השלום מפריש עצמו מן הציבור. 
כדי שיהא פנוי לעסוק בתורה ובחכמה. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב כל העוסק בתורה לשמה תורה נעשית לו סם חיים. 
שנאמר עץ חיים היא למחזיקים בה. 
וכל העוסק בתורה שלא לשמה תורה נעשית לו סם המות. 
שנאמר יערף כמטר לקחי. 
אמר רב רחמנא ליצלן מן האי דעתא. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב מאי דכתיב וידבר ה' אל משה פנים אל פנים. 
כאשר ידבר איש אל רעהו. 
מלמד שהיה הקדוש ברוך הוא מדבר עם משה בנחת. 
כדרך שאדם מדבר עם חבירו. 
אמר רב חסדא מאי דכתיב ושב אל המחנה ומשרתו יהושע בן נון נער לא ימיש מתוך האהל. 
מלמד שהיה יהושע משמש את משה בכל צרכיו. 
ולא היה זז מבית המדרש. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב אשרי מי שזוכה לשמש את החכמים. 
שעל ידי כך הוא זוכה ללמוד תורה ויראת שמים. 
ברוך הנותן ליעף כח ולאין אונים עצמה ירבה.
translation:
In the name of the Lord, we begin to write a commentary on Tractate Berakhot.

Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of that which is written, "When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, then they shall give every man a ransom for his soul to the Lord, when you number them; that there be no plague among them, when you number them" <note>Exodus 30:12</note>. 
It is taught: Rabbi Judah says, three commandments were the Israelites commanded upon their entry into the land: to appoint a king for themselves, to cut off the seed of Amalek, and to build for themselves the Chosen House <note>The Holy Temple</note>.
Rabbi Nehorai says: This passage was only said regarding the future, that they would stand in them <note>i.e., fulfill them later</note>.
And so it says, "When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number."
How is it understood that this "numbering" <term>pekudah</term> <gloss>numbering/command</gloss> is a term of importance? 
It is written here "when you number them" <term>bifkod etam</term>, and it is written there "when you number them."
Just as there it is an importance, so too here it is an importance.
Rav Ashi said: Learn from this that one who wishes to count the Israelites should not count them by the head <note>i.e., by individual tally, which is demeaning</note>.
For it is written, "that there be no plague among them when you number them."
Rav Isaac said: Anyone who counts Israel transgresses a negative commandment, as it is stated, "Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor counted" <note>Hosea 2:1</note>.
Rav Nachman bar Isaac said: There are those who say "neither measured nor counted."
It is taught: Rabbi Isaac says, what is the meaning of that which is written, "And he shall give the silver as a ransom for his soul"?
This teaches that each and every one gives half a shekel.
What is the reason? Rav Assi said: In order that they might atone for the deed of the Calf, as it is written, "And he shall give the silver as a ransom for his soul to the Lord when you number them."
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation"? 
"These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel."
Rav Hanina bar Papa said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp"?
This teaches that Moses, our teacher—peace be upon him—would separate himself from the public so that he would be free to engage in Torah and wisdom.
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: Whoever engages in Torah for its own sake, the Torah becomes for him a potion of life, as it is stated, "It is a tree of life to those who take hold of it."
And whoever engages in Torah not for its own sake, the Torah becomes for him a potion of death, as it is stated, "My doctrine shall drop as the rain."
Rav said: May the Merciful One save us from such a concept.
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And the Lord spoke unto Moses face to face, as a man speaks unto his friend"?
This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke with Moses gently, in the way that a person speaks with his friend.
Rav Chisda said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And he would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent"?
This teaches that Joshua would serve Moses in all his needs and would not move from the House of Study.
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: Happy is he who merits to serve the Sages, for through this he merits to learn Torah and fear of Heaven.
Blessed be He who gives strength to the weary and increases power to the powerless.

The first is called apparent, which is in the cognition of future things that can be known beforehand from these causes. Thus, a physician knows health or death beforehand. There is an order to such effects in knowing in some causes.

The second is prophecy improperly spoken, which communicates to someone prone to prophecy without such intelligence, according to what is held in Daniel 6: "There is need of intelligence in the vision." Jerome holds this same view in the beginning of his commentary on Isaiah. It happens that this occurs in three ways. In one way in a vision, thus Pharaoh saw ears of corn in a general way, and Belshazzar saw a hand writing on the wall (Daniel 7). The former was sleeping, the latter waking, yet neither of them was a prophet. But Daniel and Joseph, who understood the visions, were. Secondly, it happens in speech; thus Caiaphas (John 11) said a prophetic word, intending only to give counsel about the death of Christ, that it would be expedient, although he was innocent, lest the Romans come and take away their place and nation because of him. But this counsel was brought about by the Holy Spirit. He thus uttered that the death of Christ would be for the spiritual salvation of the whole world, while Caiaphas himself was ignorant of this; he was a rational animal, although through his tongue a rational word was uttered by an angel moving his tongue, without him knowing. Thirdly, this happens in operation, when the spirit moves someone to do something which has an outcome by itself, although the man moved is ignorant of the end; thus Judges 11 says of Jephthah that "the spirit of the Lord rushed upon him" to fight against the sons of Ammon, although future victory was not revealed to him. And such a motion is called the instinct of the Holy Spirit, which is a falling short of the definition of prophecy, according to the doctors, and such a motion is similar to the motion of the fortunate who moves toward something good without reason and prior knowledge, as is held in the book <term>On Good Fortune</term>. It differs, however, that the motion of the fortunate is from a natural cause, namely, from the influence of the heavens or the intelligence of the mover, as some say, or from both together, as others say. But the motion of Jephthah and Caiaphas is from a supernatural cause, namely, from the motion of the divine Spirit. This instinct approaches more closely to the definition of prophecy than the other two modes proposed. The third is prophecy true and properly spoken, which is understood as prophecy that is also found in a multiple degree, of which one is more excellent than the other; hence, for the rest, there is clearer intelligence. The first degree of this prophecy is that which, when communicated with a vision, is given with the intelligence of the vision; thus Jeremiah sees a burning pot and its face from the face of the north (Jeremiah 1), and he understood and this was signified as the army of the king of Babylon about to come to burn the city of Jerusalem.
The second degree, which is not such a vision or appearance, but hearing a voice instructing about something supernatural. 1 Kings 3: Samuel heard the voice of the Lord speaking, and yet he did not see any figure appearing to him.
